direct_text: Nicodemus is introduced as a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish council
interpretation_limit: No age family occupation history or personality is recorded

direct_text: He came to Jesus at night and addressed him as Rabbi sent from God because of the signs
interpretation_limit: The text never explains why he came at night and no motive may be assigned

direct_text: Jesus answers that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again
interpretation_limit: The Greek term also carries the sense of from above and the passage itself plays on the ambiguity

direct_text: Nicodemus asks how a grown person can be born a second time and enter the mother again
interpretation_limit: His tone is not described so confusion mockery or sincerity cannot be assigned

direct_text: Nicodemus asks how these things can be
interpretation_limit: This is his final speech in the chapter and no reply from him is recorded afterward

direct_text: Jesus notes that he is a teacher of Israel yet does not understand this
interpretation_limit: The text does not state whether the remark was rebuke or invitation

direct_text: KOERV closes the quotation mark at verse 15 and prints 16-21 without quotation marks
interpretation_limit: A KOERV footnote states that scholars differ on whether 3:16-21 is Jesus speech or the author's writing

direct_text: The narrative moves to Jesus and the disciples going to Judea
interpretation_limit: Nicodemus response decision or departure is not recorded

direct_text: Temple guards fail to arrest Jesus and Pharisees dismiss the crowd as ignorant of the law
interpretation_limit: Provides the setting for Nicodemus intervention

direct_text: John identifies him as one of them who had previously gone to meet Jesus
interpretation_limit: John links the night visit to this scene but does not state a change of heart

direct_text: Nicodemus argues their law does not judge a person before hearing him and learning what he did
interpretation_limit: He argues procedure and does not state that he believes Jesus

direct_text: They ask whether he is also from Galilee and tell him to search the scriptures
interpretation_limit: No outcome or vote is recorded and the objection is not said to succeed

direct_text: Joseph a secret disciple who feared the Jewish leaders asks Pilate for the body and takes it down
interpretation_limit: The secrecy note is written about Joseph not about Nicodemus

direct_text: Nicodemus identified as the man who had gone to Jesus at night brought about a hundred litrai of myrrh and aloes
interpretation_limit: A KOERV footnote gives the Greek as 100 litrai and about 34 kilograms and the text gives no reason for the quantity

direct_text: The two men wrap the body with the spices in linen and lay it in a new nearby tomb before the Sabbath preparation ends
interpretation_limit: The account describes a joint act and does not rank the two men

direct_text: The name Nicodemus appears only in the Gospel of John at 3:1 3:4 3:9 7:50 and 19:39
interpretation_limit: No other canonical book mentions him and nothing after the burial is recorded
